title: protect.js: check log order is the key order of STATE, so new statuses must be added to STATE in priority position
answers: why does the Protect check log list failures before successes
how do I change the order Protect prints check statuses in
I added a new status to protect.js, why does it show at the top of the check list
body:
Invariant: the order in which Protect logs checks is the key order of the STATE object. STATUS_ORDER = Object.values(STATE), and checks are sorted by STATUS_ORDER.indexOf(status) just before the console print loop.
Enforcement: .github/workflows/protect.js:module.exports (const STATE, const STATUS_ORDER, and the checks.sort call placed after the rate-limit log and before the checks.forEach print).
What breaks: reordering STATE keys silently changes the printed priority (current order is failure, pending, success, skipped). A status string that is not a key of STATE gets indexOf -1, which sorts ahead of every known status, so it appears above failures.
Fix pattern for a new status: add it to STATE at the position where it should be prioritised, rather than only emitting the string from a push site.
applies: Changes to the STATE constant or to how checks are ordered in .github/workflows/protect.js; does not cover the failure-detection logic.
says: The pull request protection log should show failed checks before pending and successful ones.
A newly created check status appears unexpectedly at the top of the summary log.
Change the sorting priority of status categories printed in the merge protection log.
Why are build check outcomes ordered with failures first in the protection report?
search: Check logging order in .github/workflows/protect.js is determined by the key order of STATE via STATUS_ORDER. Applies to changes to STATE or check sorting, where unlisted status strings evaluate to index -1 and sort above failures. New statuses must be defined in STATE at their desired priority position rather than emitted ad hoc.
